title: Meat loaf made with chicken or turkey, with tomato-based sauce

content.title: About
content.content: This meat loaf is made from ground chicken or turkey and baked under a rich tomato‑based sauce. The poultry mince is mixed with eggs, breadcrumbs, herbs and vegetables, shaped into a loaf, and baked until a golden crust forms, glazed with the tangy sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey mince contain less saturated fat than traditional beef mince.
Tomato sauce adds lycopene, a powerful antioxidant, giving the dish a bright color.
The loaf is popular in low‑calorie diets because it is high in protein and relatively low in calories.
While traditionally baked in a loaf pan, it can also be cooked in a ceramic dish for more even heat distribution.
The combination of poultry and tomatoes is a staple of Mediterranean cuisine.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with beef, poultry contains less saturated fat, supporting heart health.

items.title: Lycopene in tomato sauce
items.content: Lycopene is an antioxidant that may reduce the risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Poultry is a good source of vitamin B6 and niacin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, which support immunity and bone health.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked poultry mince can harbor salmonella or campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 165 °F (74 °C).

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chicken or turkey proteins.

items.title: Sodium in sauce
items.content: Prepared tomato sauce often contains added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: If the sauce includes sugar, the dish can raise blood glucose levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the loaf hot as a main course, slice it for sandwiches, or add pieces to salads and side dishes. It pairs well with boiled potatoes, rice, couscous or fresh vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the loaf to room temperature, then store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. For longer keeping, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven or microwave before serving.
